naslov: Worktrunk: run multiple AI agents in parallel with git worktrees | AI Tool #4
opis:
A CLI for managing git worktrees, built for running multiple AI agents in parallel. Each agent works in its own folder and on its own branch, with no collisions. Currently trending on GitHub.

How to try it:
1. `brew install worktrunk && wt config shell install`
2. `wt switch --create feature-x` creates a branch and worktree and switches you into them; launch Claude Code there
3. `wt list` shows the state of all worktrees, and `wt merge main` merges the branch and cleans up after itself

Price: Free

Official link: https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk

naslov: Qwen 3.8 reads model weights and guesses which game they learned | AI Tool #5
opis:
Reproduce part of the Weight-Space Programming paper: you give a local model a small model's weights as text, and it guesses which game that model learned. Simon Willison pulled this off with Qwen 3.8 27B.

How to try it:
1. In LM Studio, load Qwen 3.8 27B (Q4_K_M, about 17 GB) and increase the context length, since the default 8192 isn't enough
2. Install `llm` and the `llm-lmstudio` plugin
3. Take the prompt from the repo github.com/RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs (folder exp1_which_game/runs) and run `LMSTUDIO_TIMEOUT=900 llm -f <raw URL of the prompt> -m lmstudio/qwen/qwen3.8-27b`
4. Expect 45 to 65 minutes of thinking per game

Price: Free (runs locally, you need a beefy machine)

Official link: https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/3/qwen-can-interpret-model-weights/

naslov: What are open weights? AI explained in 30 seconds
opis:
Open weights means a company publishes a model's trained numbers, so anyone can download the model and run it on their own hardware. The training data and recipe usually stay secret. Example: Moonshot AI is releasing Kimi K3.1 Pro with open weights on November 4, after deliberately weakening its cyberattack skills (81% in their own test, down from 90.5%; not independently verified).
